sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Unit assessment. Work alone, show your steps, and check your work before you finish.

items.prompt: Option A has expected payoff $21 and Option B has expected payoff $30. On expected value alone, which should be chosen, and what does this criterion ignore?
choices: Neither; expected value cannot compare two options.
Option B; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Option B; expected value already accounts for risk, so nothing is ignored.
Option A; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between two people using a single fair coin flip.
choices: Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.
Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.
Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.
Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.

items.prompt: A game costs $12 to play. It pays $63 with probability 1/7 and nothing otherwise. Find the expected value to the player, and say whether the game is fair.
choices: $-12; the game is unfavourable to the player
$51; the game is favourable to the player
$-3; the game is unfavourable to the player
$9; the game is favourable to the player
